newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rocket to new intraday record.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rocket to new intraday record.

text.p: The Mexican bourse continued its recent bull run and gained sharply to a new intraday record at early afternoon trade on Tuesday.
Dealers said share prices rocketed on heavy buying by foreign investors and euphoria after mid-term elections the market saw as clean on Sunday.
The leading IPC share index was up 83.08 points, or 1.77 percent, at an historic 4,825.08.
"The market is climbing like crazy, foreigners are snapping up all they can in stocks like Kimber, Alfa, Femsa and San Luis," a desk trader said.
"Investors are expecting good second quarter earnings and euphoria over the elections is still in full swing," he added.
Heavy trading volume TV.MX of 111.9 million shares underlined the heavy flow of buyers into the market, dealers said.
Paper company Kimberly Clark de Mexico, in which Kimberly Clark Corp has a minority stake, was up 2.85 pesos at 36.60 pesos.
Conglomerate Alfa was meanwhile up 90 centavos to 55.50 pesos.
On the broad market, gainers far outpaced decliners by 67 to 29, out of a total of 113 stocks traded.
